properties.description:
At 242 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 11 miles west of
Three Points, moving northwest at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Three Points, San Pedro and Pan Tak.

This includes the following highways...
Route 86 between mile markers 131 and 152. Route 286 between mile
markers 34 and 45.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued July 28 at 5:37AM EDT until July 28 at 7:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 700 AM EDT/600 AM CDT/.

* At 537 AM EDT/437 AM CDT/, a severe thunderstorm capable of
producing waterspouts was located 9 nm south of Empire Mica Wreck,
moving south at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Cape San Blas and Empire Mica Wreck.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Frequent lightning is occurring with this storm. If caught on the
open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 28 at 4:19AM CDT until July 28 at 7:30AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Fremont County in southwestern Iowa...
South Central Cass County in southeastern Nebraska...
Northeastern Otoe County in southeastern Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 730 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 417 AM CDT, emergency management reported heavy rain in the
advisory area due to thunderstorms. Street flooding in low-lying
and poor-drainage areas is ongoing in Nebraska City. Between 1
and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Nebraska City and Camp Catron.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
At 513 AM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 9 miles southwest of Hide-A-Way Hills to 8
miles north of South Webster. Movement was southeast at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Jackson, Wellston, Mcarthur, Oak Hill, Rio Grande, Lake Hope State
Park, Hamden, Coalton, Zaleski, Vinton, Wilkesville, Mabee, Creola,
Eagle Mills, Radcliffe, Petersburg, Allensville, Byer, and
Centerpoint.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

These storms may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued July 28 at 2:44AM EDT until July 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Albany NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The mid-Hudson Valley, eastern Catskills, and the central
and southern Taconics in eastern New York, Litchfield County in
northwest Connecticut, and Berkshire County in western
Massachusetts.

* WHEN...From 2 PM EDT this afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff from heavy rainfall rates may flood
low-lying, poor drainage, urban, and other flood-prone locations.
Areas where heavy rainfall rates persist will especially be
vulnerable to flash flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of moderate to heavy rain and thunderstorms capable
of heavy downpours arrive this afternoon from west to east
and continue tonight with rainfall rates reaching or
exceeding 1 to 2 inches per hour at times.

Despite recent dry conditions, such high rainfall rates in a
short period of time can result in flash flooding, especially
in urban and poor drainage areas and where heavy rain
repeatedly impacts a given area. Steady rain continues into
Wednesday before transitioning to showers Wednesday night
into Thursday. Three day rainfall totals likely range from 1
to 3 inches with isolated amounts of 3 to 7 inches across
portions of the eastern Catskills, Litchfield County and
central and southern Taconics due to upslope enhancements.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 28 at 2:34AM EDT until July 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with heat index values up to 115
expected.

* WHERE...Portions of Big Bend and Panhandle Florida.

* WHEN...From 11 AM EDT /10 AM CDT/ this morning to 8 PM EDT /7 PM
CDT/ this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat and high humidity events, particularly for those
working or participating in outdoor activities.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sunshine, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Young children and pets should never be left unattended in vehicles
under any circumstances. This is especially true during warm or hot
weather when car interiors can reach lethal temperatures in a matter
of minutes.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening.Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

properties.areaDesc: Niagara, NY
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 28 at 2:26AM EDT until July 28 at 6:30AM EDT by NWS Buffalo NY
properties.description:
FFWBUF

The National Weather Service in Buffalo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Niagara County in western New York...

* Until 630 AM EDT.

* At 226 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lockport, Lewiston, Sanborn, Cambria Center, Ransomville and Model
City.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued July 28 at 1:20AM EDT until July 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Hampden, Hampshire and Franklin Counties in western
Massachusetts, as well as Hartford and Tolland Counties in
Northern Connecticut.

* WHEN...From this afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moderate to heavy rainfall is expected to develop Tuesday
afternoon into Wednesday across the Watch area. The heaviest
rainfall is expected Tuesday evening into Wednesday.
Excessive rainfall rates are possible, which could trigger
instances of street flooding and contribute to rises on
rivers, streams and larger river basins. Two to three inches
of rain are expected in the Watch area, with locally higher
amounts possible especially along the eastern slopes of the
Berkshires and portions of western Hartford County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

waves of 5-8 feet with sets up to 9 feet on south-southwest
facing beaches and 3-6 feet on west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 PM Wednesday
to 3 AM PDT Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 5 PM
Wednesday to 5 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Breaking waves
can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous
seas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long period southerly swell of 3 feet
at 17 seconds continues through Wednesday. A higher amplitude
swell associated with Hurricane Genevieve of around 5 feet at
14 seconds builds late Wednesday into Thursday. Swell and
associated surf look to subside late Saturday into Sunday.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued July 27 at 9:11PM PDT until August 1 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, 3-6 feet with sets to
7 feet expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5-8 feet with sets up to 9 feet on south-southwest
facing beaches and 3-6 feet on west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 PM Wednesday
to 3 AM PDT Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 5 PM
Wednesday to 5 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Breaking waves
can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous
seas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long period southerly swell of 3 feet
at 17 seconds continues through Wednesday. A higher amplitude
swell associated with Hurricane Genevieve of around 5 feet at
14 seconds builds late Wednesday into Thursday. Swell and
associated surf look to subside late Saturday into Sunday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued July 27 at 8:39PM MST until July 28 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona, including the following
areas, Baboquivari Mountains, Dragoon and Mule and Huachuca and
Santa Rita Mountains, Upper San Pedro River Valley and Upper Santa
Cruz River Valley/Altar Valley.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An organized cluster of storms or mesoscale convective system
(MCS) in northeast Sonora Mexico is expected to slowly drift
northwest across portions of south-central Arizona late this
evening and overnight tonight. This storm system will be capable
of producing moderate rainfall with pockets of very heavy
rainfall. Although widespread rainfall amounts between 0.50 and
1.00 inches are anticipated, localized rainfall amounts between 1
and 3 inches will be possible resulting in localized flash
flooding. The heaviest rainfall is expected over the southwest
half of Santa Cruz county and extreme south-central Pima county
and may have significant impact on the Nogales Wash overnight.
Heavy rainfall Monday evening along Highway 286 and along and
Arivaca Road have made portions of south central Pima county
vulnerable to flash flooding with additional rainfall overnight.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.description:
The following message is transmitted in collaboration with the
Wyoming Department of Environmental Quality, Air Quality Division,
and the Wyoming Department of Health.

* WHAT...Air Quality Alert for Wildfire Smoke.

* WHERE...Northeast Wyoming.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Poor air quality due to wildfire smoke.
properties.instruction:
The Wyoming Department of Health recommends the elderly, young
children, and individuals with respiratory problems avoid excessive
physical exertion and minimize outdoor activities during this time.

particulate matter and ozone, which can cause respiratory health
effect. Although these people are most susceptible to health
impacts, the Department of Health also advises that everyone should
avoid prolonged exposure to poor air quality conditions.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued July 27 at 3:03PM HST until July 29 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING FOR EAST FACING SHORES THROUGH WEDNESDAY
AFTERNOON...

.A east swell from Hurricane Fausto will continue to build
tonight and peak Tuesday above High Surf Warning levels. The swell
will decline on Wednesday as the system passes to the northwest.

* WHAT...Surf building to 14 to 18 feet.

* WHERE...East Facing shores.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Very High. Expect ocean water surging and sweeping
across beaches, coastal benches, and lava flows creating the
potential for impacts to coastal properties and infrastructure,
including roadways. Powerful longshore and rip currents will be
present at most beaches. Large breaking waves and strong
currents may impact harbor entrances and channels causing
challenging boat handling.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 27 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River At Cotulla affecting La Salle County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers...
Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CDT Monday the stage was 7.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
Wednesday afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 40.3 feet
early Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 40.2
feet on 07/13/2002.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Bristol Bay Coast; Inland Bristol Bay; Lake Iliamna / Nila Vena / Nanvarpak
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 27 at 3:01PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
Daytime temperatures will reach 70 to 75 degrees later this week,
and will be hottest on Wednesday and Thursday. Temperatures this
warm, and for this long, happen about once per year.

The long duration of warmer days may impact subsistence
activities like berry picking, fishing, and hunting. This could
also affect people who are extremely sensitive to heat (like
elders or infants), especially if they are unable to cool down or
stay hydrated.

Actions: Keep homes cool by closing curtains during the day and
opening windows at night. If outdoors, stay hydrated and dress in
lighter and looser clothing. Be alert to signs of heat stress in
yourself and others.

NWSheadline: WARMER THAN USUAL TEMPERATURES FROM TUESDAY THROUGH FRIDAY

properties.areaDesc: Crook, OR; Gilliam, OR; Grant, OR; Jefferson, OR; Morrow, OR; Umatilla, OR; Union, OR; Wallowa, OR; Wasco, OR; Wheeler, OR
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 27 at 2:52PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air Quality
Advisory until noon PDT Wednesday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Advisory, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

For additional information...please visit the Web site at
http://www.oregon.gov/DEQ
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued July 27 at 2:27PM PDT until August 1 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and elevated surf.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is an increased risk of ocean
drowning due to hazardous rip currents. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SATURDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued July 27 at 2:27PM PDT until July 29 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 8 feet with dangerous
rip currents, highest across south facing beaches exposed to
southerly swells.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 PM Wednesday
to 3 AM PDT Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 5 PM
Wednesday to 5 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of sea water is likely around the time of
high tide, over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such as
parking lots, beaches, and walkways. Significant damage to
roads or structures is NOT expected. There is an increased
risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and
surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury,
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of 6.2 to near 7.0 feet will
occur in the evening hours through Friday night, peaking
tonight through Thursday night. In conjunction with the
highest expected surf from the Hurricane Genevieve southerly
swell, the best potential for minor coastal flooding impacts
is expected Wednesday and Thursday evening.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 27 at 2:52PM MDT until July 28 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Temperatures of 105 to 107 expected.

* WHERE...Much of south-central New Mexico, including the
Mesilla and Hatch Valleys, and the western Tularosa Basin.
This includes the city of Las Cruces. Also, in Texas...most of
El Paso County, the Lower Valley through Hudsepth County, and
the Salt Basin including Dell City.

* WHEN...This afternoon to 9 PM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out
of the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young
children and pets should never be left unattended in vehicles
under any circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when
possible. To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational
Safety and Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent
rest breaks in shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone
overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded location.
Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

NWSheadline: HEAT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT THIS AFTERNOON TO 9 PM MDT TUESDAY

properties.description:

combined seas 7 to 10 ft expected when conditions are worst.

* WHERE...Portions of the coastal waters of southwest
California.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 3 PM PDT this
afternoon. For the Gale Warning, until 3 AM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will create dangerous sea conditions
which could capsize or damage small and large vessels.

for more.
properties.instruction:

Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 27 at 11:54AM MST until August 2 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions, with temperatures around 106 to
112 expected below 4000 feet.

* WHERE...Yavapai County Valleys and Basins.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 8 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected below 4000 feet, with
daytime temperatures ranging around 100 degrees at Havasupai
Gardens, and 112 to 116 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 8 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM THURSDAY TO 8 PM MST SUNDAY BELOW 4000 FEET

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 27 at 12:38PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...High concentration of smoke particulates from wildfire
smoke.

* WHERE...Baker, Harney, and Malheur Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE.

* IMPACTS...Smoke can irritate the eyes, lungs and worsen some
medical conditions. People most at risk to adverse health effects
include infants, young children, people with heart or lung
disease, older adults, and pregnant women.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on
weather. Check current conditions on the Oregon Smoke Information
Blog, DEQ's Air Quality Index, or by downloading the free
OregonAIR app on your smartphone.
properties.instruction:
* Stay inside if possible. Keep windows and doors closed.

* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity.

* Use high efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters in indoor
ventilation systems or portable air purifiers.

* Be aware of smoke in your area and avoid places with the highest
levels.

* If you have heart or lung disease, or asthma, follow your
healthcare provider's advice.

For current Oregon air quality conditions, please visit:
https://aqi.oregon.gov

For additional information, please visit:
https://www.oregon.gov/deq
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 27 at 12:33PM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
The following message is transmitted on behalf of the Wyoming
Department of Environmental Quality, Air Quality Division, and the
Wyoming Department of Health.

* WHAT...Air Quality Alert for Wildfire Smoke.

* WHERE...Northern Johnson County.

* WHEN...1 PM MDT Monday through 1 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Smoke from Oregon, Idaho, and Montana fires enter
northern Wyoming late Monday through Tuesday. Smoke could limited
visibilities at times.

HEALTH INFORMATION...The Wyoming Department of Health recommends
that the elderly, young children, and individuals with respiratory
problems avoid excessive physical exertion and minimize outdoor
activities during this time. Wildfire smoke is made up of a variety
of pollutants, including particulate matter and ozone, which can
cause respiratory health effects. Although these people are most
susceptible to health impacts, the Department of Health also advises
that everyone should avoid prolonged exposure to poor air quality
conditions.

CURRENT CONDITIONS...The Wyoming Department of Environmental
Quality, Air Quality Division offers near real-time air quality data
for Wyoming's monitoring stations and health effects information to
help the public interpret current conditions. Current air quality
conditions across the state of Wyoming can be found at
http://www.wyvisnet.com/.

properties.description:
The  Washington State Department of Ecology, Benton Clean Air
Agency has issued an Air Quality Alert until 11 AM PDT this morning.

For the Smoke Air Quality Alert, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.

levels.

healthcare provider's advice.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 27 at 8:43AM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
AQAMT

The Montana Department of Environmental Quality has issued an air
quality alert for Blaine, Cascade, Chouteau, Deer Lodge, Fergus,
Glacier, Granite, Hill, Judith Basin, Lake, Lewis and Clark,
Liberty, Missoula, Petroleum, Pondera, Powell, Ravalli, Silver Bow,
Teton, Toole, Phillips counties in effect until 9AM on 07/28/2026 An
Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending upwards
and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air Quality
Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near future.

Elevated particulate levels from wildfire smoke

As of 6AM on 07/27/2026, particulate levels in Havre and Malta are
Unhealthy.

As of 6AM on 07/27/2026, particulate levels in Butte, Great Falls,
Hamilton, Helena, Lewistown and Sleeping Giant are Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups.

As of 6AM on 07/27/2026, particulate levels in Columbia Falls, Cut
Bank, Dillon, Frenchtown, Libby, Missoula and Thompson Falls are
Moderate.

When air quality is Unhealthy... State and local health officials
recommend that people with respiratory or heart disease, the elderly,
and children should avoid prolonged exertion; everyone else should
limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups... State and local
health officials recommend that people with respiratory or heart
disease, the elderly and children should limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

For more information visit the Montana Department of Environmental
Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
